issueComments.body:
Source analysis and implementation design (planning only)

**Authority and evidence boundary.** The direct human request delegated through coordinator task `01a0f838-69d6-75b3-8cc0-f768175aa03e` is: "board and individual-card editor language selection changes speech generation but text stays English. After translations are generated, language selection should expose that language's editable translation; manual corrections must persist and regenerate pronunciation from corrected text." This task is authorized to scope and file one issue only. The inspected authenticated live master and clean local clone both resolve to `1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4`. No app run, runtime reproduction, test execution, package installation or implementation is claimed. The user's installed/served build and exact control path remain unknown.

**What current source establishes**

- [BoardEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx#L23-L39) has no active editing-language state; its [preview](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardEditor.tsx#L58-L64) maps raw `board.tiles` to `TileFace` and opens that raw card. [BoardLanguages](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/BoardLanguages.tsx#L49-L81) configures enabled play languages, switchable cards and label-switch behavior, prepares missing translations and displays a read-only review. Enabling a language is not currently selecting an editor variant.
- [TileEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/TileEditor.tsx#L73-L95) keeps its main fields/preview on the source draft. Its prominent "Language for this tile" controls write `draft.language`; they do not translate or select a saved translation. Separate lower buttons for board-following cards set `audioLanguage` and expose translated label/speech fields. That target starts null, so it does not inherit the board's selected language. This split explains a source-level mismatch with the requested interaction; it does not prove which control or build produced the report.
- Translation correction is already partly supported. The [existing browser scenario](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/tests/web/app.spec.ts#L383-L448) prepares Russian, selects the lower translation button, changes spoken text, checks the matching TTS request, saves and exercises offline playback. It was read, not run. Do not describe master as lacking all translation editing or correction persistence.
- [Stored translations](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/schema.ts#L17-L42) contain `language`, `label`, `speech` and a `source` signature of normalized base label, speech and language. They have no manual-edit provenance. [Resolution and preparation](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/boardLanguages.ts#L27-L108) canonicalize language tags, ignore stale source signatures, preserve fixed cards, request only missing variants, validate exact response pairs and reject mismatched board revisions. Missing/stale play variants retain the original text **and original language**, which is safer than retagging English.
- Preservation gaps are visible in code: [TileEditor](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/ui/TileEditor.tsx#L38-L48) filters stale translations on save and filters unselected/stale entries while editing another translation. `applyTranslations` likewise filters retained entries for touched cards. [AI proposal application](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/schema.ts#L171-L195) retains matching old translations only when the proposal does not supply the same language; supplied entries take precedence and the merged list is sliced to six. Therefore existing guards do not by themselves guarantee preservation of manual corrections across all preparation, source-edit and AI-edit paths. These are source-derived risks, not runtime loss claims.

**Persistence, audio and asynchronous contracts to preserve**

[App's board change callback](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx#L125-L139) resolves the latest board, advances its revision and records undo; the card editor supplies a whole tile and closes after an optimistic change. [useLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/useLibrary.ts#L33-L64) serializes writes, exposes save failure/retry and has a durable commit path. [Native SQLite](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/storage.ts#L20-L28) and [browser IndexedDB](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/data/storage.web.ts#L15-L24) persist the validated library including translations. Keep the draft/correction available after a failed write; never infer durable success from the closed sheet or from audio readiness. Guard same-card concurrent changes before applying an old whole-tile draft.

The audio pipeline already has the right identity: [speechKey](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/speech.ts#L9-L21) uses trimmed NFC text plus canonical BCP-47 language. [SpeechLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/services/speechLibrary.ts#L38-L106) captures the requested input, deduplicates jobs and stores completion under that key independently of board revisions. [useSpeechLibrary](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/services/useSpeechLibrary.ts#L19-L47) verifies the response key before saving, respects consent/automatic-audio settings and retries recovery; both platforms persist the key-to-clip mapping. [Server caching](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/server/src/speech-cache.ts#L44-L80) also binds synthesis profile and uses immutable clip IDs, replacing its pointer only after success. [Synthesis](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/server/src/synthesis.ts#L57-L76) requests the supplied words and language without translation and checks the transcript. Reuse these contracts; a tile-ID-only cache or global cache deletion is unnecessary.

For changed spoken text, show missing/preparing/error for the **new key** and never reuse the old phrase's clip. A label-only correction can retain matching speech audio. For a fresh take of identical text/language, the existing valid clip can remain available if regeneration fails; for changed text, fallback must speak the corrected text in its matching language. Retain sound-check behavior when no suitable device voice exists.

**Proposed change boundaries**

1. Add a shared explicit editing-language selector in the existing board/card workflow, initialized from the board/play context when available. Show translated labels in the editor even if the separate play setting intentionally keeps source labels. Resolve presentation and audio from a variant while keeping the original card object/ID for edits; never save a resolved display tile over the source. Fixed cards stay visibly fixed. Keep source-language metadata editing distinct.
2. Keep per-language draft fields when switching, including incomplete input; apply existing required-label/speech validation on Save without losing the draft. Distinguish a missing translation from a stale translation retained for review. Selecting languages must not filter other entries. Preserve source text and corrected variants, and make source-change review/replacement deliberate. If correction provenance is added, use a small backward-compatible optional field and conservatively protect existing entries of unknown origin; do not let schema parsing strip it. Respect existing bounded language/storage limits without silently evicting a correction.
3. Merge generated translations into only the requested missing variants. Require an explicit reviewed replacement before an AI proposal supersedes a protected correction. A changed source marks old corrections for review rather than dropping or silently refreshing them. Preserve unrelated languages, media, IDs, order and undo.
4. Retain the existing board-revision checks and AbortController lifecycle; add draft/request generation identity where unsaved edits are not represented by the saved revision. Before applying any result, check the original board/card/source and target. Closing, cancelling, switching cards or restarting a request must invalidate obsolete UI callbacks. Audio may finish safely in its original cache key; it must not alter the active fields, switch the selected language or falsely mark another input ready. Stop preview playback when its displayed text/language changes.
5. Extend the existing [core language tests](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/packages/core/src/boardLanguages.test.ts), [speech-library tests](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/apps/mobile/src/services/speechLibrary.test.ts) and [browser speech tests](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/1f0329052bd46b1e953c5adb5ad7e59ba2f2dcc4/tests/web/speech.spec.ts), rather than rebuilding their coverage. Use an English source plus two translations, a fixed card and an initially missing variant. Check both editor entry paths; label-only versus spoken corrections; switching with an incomplete draft; save/reopen/reload and failed-write retry; source-change review; unrelated AI proposals; translation and TTS responses completed out of order; cancellation/offline recovery. Inspect actual TTS payloads and playback, not merely a ready badge. Eventual UI evidence belongs in the PR under the pinned standards; no implementation evidence is duplicated here.

**Coordination and disposition**

#31 owns balanced geometry; #30 owns the parent hold, navigation and animated editor handoff. Reuse stable card IDs and their settled/pinned preview geometry; pass selected language and preserve draft/save state through the #30 handoff. These are shared-file integration concerns, not proof that translations require either feature first. Coordinator chooses sequencing or a pinned parent; no new branch owner is assigned here.

Open PR #29 belongs to account implementation task `01a10f7a-bf1e-7154-8695-468b946d4021`; it changes App, storage/useLibrary, schema and adds speech-cache reload. Preserve its backup/restoration contracts if it lands; it is not a feature prerequisite. #20's grants remain deferred and #28's playback diagnosis remains separate. All existing open/closed issue titles and open PR paths were checked; no duplicate translation outcome was found. Current nearby issue discussions and PR conversation/review/inline collections were retrieved; account-flow and grant feedback remain with their existing owners, with no readiness reassessment here.

Read the supplied agentic-development-workflow requirements instructions, repository AGENTS, pinned deployment/intake/template, live Calibrate #405 and all twelve specified amendments. Execution `f0919b184b6344d6279178b2388190936ca432a9` and communication `97e5583c8355f3673aad0835c0ce3ca1486aeb8b` remain unchanged; the direct five-section issue amendment governs this body. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Review source-language collisions with saved corrections**

When an AI proposal changes an existing board-following card’s source language to the language of a protected correction (for example, `en-US` to `ru-RU`) and omits that language from `tile.translations`, this blindly retains the correction without reporting a replacement. `proposalTranslationReplacements` therefore returns no review item, while `tileInLanguage` chooses the new source words whenever the selected language equals `tile.language`, silently replacing the corrected Russian text and audio in actual use. Treat this source-language collision as a protected replacement or otherwise prevent the new source from shadowing the saved correction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in `a08a723d87cee4bbb3026f11b3fcfa8c63c6f2ce`. An AI source-language change is now refused when it would shadow a saved manual/legacy translation, including when the proposal omits translations and when ordinary replacement review was approved. The error directs the parent to keep the source language and edit its translation. A core regression passes; a browser regression verifies refusal leaves every saved tile unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block manual source-language collisions**

When a board-following card has a protected Russian translation and a parent changes its original language from English to Russian here, the translation is retained but becomes unreachable: `tileInLanguage` returns the source tile whenever the selected language equals `tile.language`, so playback silently uses the newly relabeled original words instead of the saved correction. The AI path now guards this collision, but this manual path does not; reject the language change or require explicit handling when a protected translation already uses the new source language.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
